title: Paranal laser
caption: A laser guide star beam under the southern Milky Way, Paranal
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A laser beam rises from the Very Large Telescope into the sky over Paranal, while the southern Milky Way crosses overhead. The constellation of Carina is among those along its path. The photograph is by Petr Horálek.
The beam works as an artificial star. Astronomers use it to correct for disturbance in the atmosphere, the shifting of the air that makes stars twinkle and blurs the images a telescope records.

The idea is that the telescope watches the artificial star, measures how the atmosphere distorts it, and then adjusts to cancel out that distortion for the real objects under study. Because the laser can be pointed where the astronomers need it, the correction does not depend on a bright natural star happening to lie nearby. The result is sharper observations from a telescope on the ground.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph by Petr Horálek for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and the laser beam look brighter here than to someone standing on the mountain.
